project.name: Kill Switch
project.tagline: An accountability layer for teams of autonomous agents: who did what, stop them fast, undo only their damage.
project.event: SEED Hackathon 2026 — The Age of Autonomy · Sub-theme 03: Agent Safety
brief: Ten agents are working. One just broke something. What changed, who changed it, how fast can it be undone?
Build: per-agent identity on every action, live monitoring, containment.
Rollback that reverses one agent's damage without discarding the other agents' work.
Scored on time-to-identify, time-to-contain and clean recovery.
Jury rewards the best problem framing; agents must be auditable, not just demoable; juries will try to break it.

meetings.title: Call #1 — Research readout and decisions
meetings.summary: Research confirms that undo is a dependency problem. Airlock already does forward containment; our niche is the backward half (revert one agent's landed writes, repair their readers), an authenticated record, and oracle-scored recovery. All 13 open questions resolved; Sprint 2 opened.
decisions: Headline layered: problem = undo breaks once others read the bad write; fix = provenance; payoff = selective undo; why = testimony vs evidence (Aarav to confirm)
Own row-versioned SQLite store; Dolt only as the production twin
Re-run deterministic steps through the outbox with idempotency keys; LLM steps become approval-gated re-plan items
Tamper-evident up to the last witnessed head: hash chain + two signatures + separate witness + verify
A bad signature suspends the connection, never the claimed agent
Hold per action, using only recorded read sets
Gateway is the scheduler (tick barrier) so runs are deterministic and recovery scores reproduce
Hero scenario F2+: supplier IBAN swap → billing/payments/comms; triage conflict; inventory/docs independent
next: Abstract Kit for Aarav (fact card, guardrails, diagram, term lock, jury Q&A)
Walking skeleton with the determinism test

decisions.title: Rollback is a dependency problem, not a snapshot problem
decisions.summary: Confirmed by RES-01/02/04/06. Two claims killed: 'nobody has provenance containment' and 'nobody has agent undo'.

decisions.title: Layered headline: dependency gap → provenance → selective undo
decisions.summary: Problem first (organisers' order); provenance as the fix; selective undo as the demo payoff; testimony vs evidence as why it matters.

decisions.title: Own row-versioned SQLite store
decisions.summary: Dolt never run and outside our dependency list; shown as the production twin.

decisions.title: Re-run deterministic, re-plan LLM with approval
decisions.summary: LLM replay does not transfer (RES-01). Re-runs go through the outbox, deduplicated by idempotency key.

decisions.title: Tamper-evident to last witnessed head
decisions.summary: Hash chain, agent and gateway signatures, separate witness process, verify CLI. Never 'tamper-proof'.

decisions.title: Bad signature suspends the connection, not the claimed agent
decisions.summary: Stops forgers from framing honest agents (Kabir).

decisions.title: Per-action lineage hold from recorded read sets
decisions.summary: Independent work keeps running; agent-declared lineage is never trusted.

decisions.title: Gateway is the scheduler (tick barrier)
decisions.summary: Same seed → byte-identical records, so oracle scores reproduce for the jury.

decisions.title: Honest-claims rules for the abstract
decisions.summary: No 'first', no Airlock comparison, no 'tamper-proof'/'compliant', Who&When quoted with its setting, our numbers labelled targets.
